literature.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 蛋白质组学和功能分析表明,DPEV 将巨噬细胞重新编程为促炎和焦亡倾向状态。与物理破坏产生的囊泡相比,DPEV 显示出增强的免疫刺激能力。 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014887]
在缺乏 I 型和 II 型干扰素受体的 SFTSV 感染小鼠中,在感染后 24、48 或 72 小时开始口服 molnupiravir 死亡率(100 mg/kg,每天两次,持续 3 天),可延迟 死亡率 并降低中位血液病毒 RNA 载量。然而,每个治疗组的 6 只小鼠中只有一只存活到感染后 12 天。 [10.1016/j.virusres.2026.199844]
长角血蜱的季节性活动在不同地点基本上是同步的,若虫在春季达到高峰,成虫在夏季达到高峰,幼虫在秋季达到高峰,而在冬季则没有可检测到的活动。人类 发热伴血小板减少综合征 病例表现出不同的季节性模式,根据地点的不同,高峰出现在 5 月、7 月或 10 月。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11002836/v1]
798例SFTSV感染患者中,271例(34.0%)病情发展为危重,其中137例(50.6%)在住院期间死亡。危重患者表现出更明显的血液学和凝血异常、器官损伤的生化证据以及泌尿系统异常,特别是蛋白尿、血尿和糖尿。在重症患者中,非幸存者比幸存者有更严重的器官功能障碍和更高的疾病严重程度评分。 [10.3389/fcimb.2026.1996009]
我们的研究结果表明,甘油磷脂代谢是SFTSV感染的Huh7细胞和发热伴血小板减少综合征患者中最显着破坏的途径,溶血磷脂酰胆碱(LPC)种类,包括LPC(16:1)、LPC(18:1)、LPC(16:0)和LPC(18:0),表现出水平下降。 [10.1128/msphere.00557-26]

literature.headline_en: Recent Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Proteomic and functional analyses demonstrated that DPEVs reprogram macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory and pyroptosis-prone state. DPEVs displayed enhanced immunostimulatory capacity compared with vesicles generated by physical disruption. [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014887]

In SFTSV-infected mice lacking type I and type II interferon receptors, oral molnupiravir treatment (100 mg/kg twice daily for 3 days), initiated at 24, 48, or 72 h post-infection, delayed mortality and reduced median blood viral RNA loads. [10.1016/j.virusres.2026.199844]

The seasonal activity of Haemaphysalis longicornis was largely synchronous across locations, with nymphs peaking in spring, adults in summer, larvae in fall, and no detectable activity during winter. Human SFTS cases showed diverse seasonal patterns, with peaks in May, July, or October depending on the location. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11002836/v1]
Of 798 patients with SFTSV infection, 271 (34.0%) developed critical illness, of whom 137 (50.6%) died during hospitalization. [10.3389/fcimb.2026.1996009]

Our findings revealed that glycerophospholipid metabolism was the most significantly disrupted pathway in both SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and SFTS patients, with lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) species, including LPC(16:1), LPC(18:1), LPC(16:0), and LPC(18:0), showing decreased levels. [10.1128/msphere.00557-26]

key_findings_zh: 发表在《Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology》上的一项回顾性多中心研究报告称,尿胆原阳性、血清肌酐升高和高龄是 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 感染危重患者住院 死亡率 的独立预后标志物。该研究还确定了血液学和凝血异常、器官损伤的生化证据以及泌尿异常作为严重临床轨迹的指标。 [news-fb2f65daa24f25dc]

papers.title: Preclinical evaluation of NHC and molnupiravir against severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus.
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonotic disease caused by severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV). The disease can be severe or fatal in companion animals. In veterinary medicine, no specific treatment has been established for SFTS, and management is limited to supportive care. To investigate the antiviral potential of molnupiravir against SFTSV, we evaluated the activity of its ribonucleoside metabolite, β-D-N 4 -hydroxycytidine (NHC), in feline- and canine-derived cells and the effects of oral molnupiravir on survival and blood viral RNA loads in a lethal mouse model. NHC inhibited the production of infectious SFTSV in all four cell lines tested, with plaque assay-based 50% effective concentrations of 0.33-0.97 μM. In SFTSV-infected mice lacking type I and type II interferon receptors, oral molnupiravir treatment (100 mg/kg twice daily for 3 days), initiated at 24, 48, or 72 h post-infection, delayed mortality and reduced median blood viral RNA loads. However, only one of six mice in each treated group survived to 12 days post-infection. At 6 days post-infection, median blood viral RNA loads in treated groups were 0.57%-1.59% of the median load in vehicle controls, with significant reductions when treatment was initiated at 24 or 48 h. In a separate experiment, extending treatment to 5 or 7 days did not demonstrate a clear additional survival benefit. These findings demonstrate antiviral activity in companion animal-derived cells and delayed mortality in an interferon-receptor-deficient mouse model. Further studies are required to establish therapeutic efficacy in naturally infected cats.

source_records.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonotic disease caused by severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV). The disease can be severe or fatal in companion animals. In veterinary medicine, no specific treatment has been established for SFTS, and management is limited to supportive care. To investigate the antiviral potential of molnupiravir against SFTSV, we evaluated the activity of its ribonucleoside metabolite, β-D-N 4 -hydroxycytidine (NHC), in feline- and canine-derived cells and the effects of oral molnupiravir on survival and blood viral RNA loads in a lethal mouse model. NHC inhibited the production of infectious SFTSV in all four cell lines tested, with plaque assay-based 50% effective concentrations of 0.33-0.97 μM. In SFTSV-infected mice lacking type I and type II interferon receptors, oral molnupiravir treatment (100 mg/kg twice daily for 3 days), initiated at 24, 48, or 72 h post-infection, delayed mortality and reduced median blood viral RNA loads. However, only one of six mice in each treated group survived to 12 days post-infection. At 6 days post-infection, median blood viral RNA loads in treated groups were 0.57%-1.59% of the median load in vehicle controls, with significant reductions when treatment was initiated at 24 or 48 h. In a separate experiment, extending treatment to 5 or 7 days did not demonstrate a clear additional survival benefit. These findings demonstrate antiviral activity in companion animal-derived cells and delayed mortality in an interferon-receptor-deficient mouse model. Further studies are required to establish therapeutic efficacy in naturally infected cats.

papers.abstract_zh: 严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 是一种由 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 引起的新出现的 蜱媒 人畜共患疾病。这种疾病对于伴侣动物来说可能是严重的甚至是致命的。在兽医学中,尚未针对发热伴血小板减少综合征制定具体的治疗,管理仅限于支持性护理。为了研究 molnupiravir 对抗 SFTSV 的 抗病毒药物 潜力,我们评估了其核糖核苷代谢物 β-D-N 4 -羟基胞苷 (NHC) 在猫和犬源性细胞中的活性,以及​​口服 molnupiravir 对致死小鼠模型中存活和血液病毒 RNA 载量的影响。NHC 抑制了所有四种测试细胞系中感染性 SFTSV 的产生,基于噬菌斑测定的 50% 有效浓度为 0.33-0.97 μM。在缺乏 I 型和 II 型干扰素受体的 SFTSV 感染小鼠中,在感染后 24、48 或 72 小时开始口服 molnupiravir 死亡率(100 mg/kg,每天两次,持续 3 天),可延迟 死亡率 并降低中位血液病毒 RNA 载量。然而,每个治疗组的 6 只小鼠中只有一只存活到感染后 12 天。感染后 6 天,治疗组的中位血液病毒 RNA 载量为媒介物对照组中位载量的 0.57%-1.59%,当在 24 或 48 小时开始 治疗 时显着降低。在一项单独的实验中,将 治疗 延长至 5 或 7 天并没有表现出明显的额外生存益处。这些发现证明了 死亡率 在伴侣动物源性细胞中的活性,并在干扰素受体缺陷的小鼠模型中延迟了 死亡率 的活性。需要进一步的研究来确定对自然感染的猫的治疗效果。

papers.title: Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles aggravate macrophagic pyroptosis in Dabie bandavirus infection
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease causing remarkably increased morbidity and mortality in East Asia. Thrombocytopenia is a hallmark pathogenic event in SFTS, clinical feature and an independent predictor of multi-organ failure and poor clinical outcomes. Although Dabie bandavirus (DBV) can bind to and replicate within platelets, the contribution of activated platelets to SFTS pathogenesis remains elusive. Here, we identify platelet-derived extracellular vesicles induced by DBV (DPEVs) as critical mediators of immune dysregulation. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (DPEVs) in the pathogenesis of Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS) caused by Dabie bandavirus (DBV). These results highlight DPEVs as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for SFTS. The study's high confidence is supported by proteomic and functional analyses, though limitations in generalizability and potential confounding factors remain.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是一种新出现的 蜱媒 传染病,在东亚导致发病率和 死亡率 显着增加。该研究旨在探讨血小板源性细胞外囊泡在发热伴血小板减少综合征的发病机制中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究针对大别班达病毒(DBV)感染进行,重点关注血小板源性细胞外囊泡(DPEV)对巨噬细胞焦亡和炎症反应的影响。该研究涉及 DPEV 的蛋白质组学和功能分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用蛋白质组学和功能分析来评估 DPEV 对巨噬细胞的影响。该研究将 DPEV 与物理破坏产生的囊泡进行比较,以评估它们的免疫刺激能力。
elements_zh.main_results: 蛋白质组学和功能分析表明,DPEV 将巨噬细胞重新编程为促炎和焦亡倾向状态。与物理破坏产生的囊泡相比,DPEV 显示出增强的免疫刺激能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: DBV激活的血小板释放丰富的细胞外囊泡,直接诱导巨噬细胞焦亡并显着放大病毒驱动的炎症反应。这些发现定义了一个先前未被认识的致病轴,该轴将 DBV 感染期间的血小板激活、细胞外囊泡信号传导、线粒体损伤和巨噬细胞焦亡联系起来。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DPEV 作为炎症的关键放大器,在 发热伴血小板减少综合征 中提供血小板减少症和疾病严重程度之间的机制联系,突出了它们作为生物标志物和治疗靶点的潜在价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于使用了蛋白质组和功能分析,该研究对其研究结果提供了很高的可信度,但它没有解决潜在的混杂因素或对其他人群的普遍性。

media_mentions.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection by November 24, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Extracellular vesicles released by platelets during Dabie bandavirus infection directly trigger macrophage pyroptosis and amplify inflammatory responses, according to findings published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Dabie bandavirus causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, an emerging tick-borne infectious disease characterized by remarkably increased morbidity and mortality across East Asia. In clinical settings, thrombocytopenia represents a hallmark pathogenic event and an established independent predictor of multi-organ failure and poor clinical outcomes. Although Dabie bandavirus is known to bind to and replicate within host platelets, the precise contribution of activated platelets to disease pathogenesis has remained elusive. The researchers identified platelet-derived extracellular vesicles induced by Dabie bandavirus, designated DPEVs, as critical mediators of immune dysregulation. Upon viral activation, platelets release abundant vesicles that markedly heighten virus-driven inflammation while driving recipient macrophages into a distinct pro-inflammatory and pyroptosis-prone state. When compared directly with extracellular vesicles generated through physical disruption, DPEVs displayed significantly enhanced immunostimulatory capacity. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Mechanistically, the study showed that DPEVs compromise mitochondrial integrity and stimulate the production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species inside macrophages, thereby triggering the downstream pyroptotic death program. This sequence defines a previously unrecognized pathogenic axis linking viral platelet activation, extracellular vesicle signaling, mitochondrial injury, and macrophagic pyroptosis during Dabie bandavirus infection. Beyond promoting inflammatory damage, DPEVs incorporated viral components, suggesting a potential dual role in mediating both inflammatory amplification and viral dissemination. By establishing a direct mechanistic link between thrombocytopenia and clinical severity in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, the findings position these virus-induced extracellular vesicles as key amplifiers of inflammation with notable potential value as clinical biomarkers and therapeutic targets. papers.title: Seasonality of Haemaphysalis longicornis and its implications for the transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus: a modelling study
papers.abstract: Background The Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, is the primary vector of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), an emerging infectious disease rapidly spreading in Asia with a case-fatality rate of up to 30%. Understanding the seasonal activity of H. longicornis is critical for elucidating SFTS epidemiology and improving risk prediction. Methods We compiled databases of life stage-specific seasonal activity data for H. longicornis, as well as laboratory-derived developmental durations under different temperature conditions, from the published literature. We then developed an empirical model integrating laboratory observations with field temperature data to predict interstadial and full-generation developmental durations across 20 locations with observed tick seasonality, seven SFTS transmission hotspots, and three locations without reported H. longicornis presence. Finally, we inferred the cohort structures underlying observed H. longicornis seasonal patterns by integrating observed seasonality with model-predicted developmental durations. Results Despite substantial variation in annual mean temperature (7.3–17.4°C), the seasonal activity of H. longicornis was largely synchronous across locations, with nymphs peaking in spring, adults in summer, larvae in fall, and no detectable activity during winter, potentially attributable to the substantially higher overwinter survival of nymphs than of other life stages. In contrast, human SFTS cases exhibited diverse seasonal patterns, with peaks occurring in May, July, or October depending on the location, suggesting that variation in human-tick contact patterns may play an important role in shaping the observed seasonality of human SFTS. The predicted full-generation developmental duration was 1–2 years in locations with observed H. longicornis seasonality or reported human SFTS cases, but < 1 year in locations without known H. longicornis presence under most examined scenarios. Inferred cohort structures showed that a single seasonal activity peak may comprise multiple overlapping cohorts. For example, the summer adult peak from May to August likely consists of overwintered adults for the early part, and newly matured adults that fed as nymphs in the spring for the latter part. Conclusions These findings highlight the need to consider human-tick contact patterns and location- and month-specific temporal scales when modelling human SFTS risk.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景亚洲长角蜱(Haemaphysalis longicornis)是严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)的主要媒介,这是一种在亚洲迅速传播的新发传染病,病死率高达30%。了解 H. longicornis 的季节性活动对于阐明 发热伴血小板减少综合征 流行病学 和改进风险预测至关重要。方法 我们根据已发表的文献,编制了长角长角虫生命阶段特定季节性活动数据的数据库,以及不同温度条件下实验室得出的发育持续时间。然后,我们开发了一个经验模型,将实验室观察与现场温度数据相结合,以预测 20 个观察到蜱季节性的地点、七个 发热伴血小板减少综合征 传播 热点以及三个没有报告长角蜱存在的地点的间期和全代发育持续时间。最后,我们通过将观察到的季节性与模型预测的发育持续时间相结合,推断出观察到的 H. longicornis 季节模式背后的 队列研究 结构。结果 尽管年平均气温(7.3–17.4°C)存在很大差异,但不同地点的长角长角蝽的季节性活动基本上是同步的,若虫在春季达到高峰,成虫在夏季,幼虫在秋季,而在冬季没有可检测到的活动,这可能归因于若虫的越冬存活率远高于其他生命阶段。相比之下,人类 发热伴血小板减少综合征 病例表现出不同的季节性模式,根据地点的不同,高峰出现在 5 月、7 月或 10 月,这表明人类与蜱接触模式的变化可能在形成观察到的人类 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的季节性方面发挥着重要作用。在观察到 H. longicornis 季节性或报告的人类 发热伴血小板减少综合征 病例的地区,预测的全代发育持续时间为 1-2 年,但在大多数检查情况下,在不知道 H. longicornis 存在的地区,预测的全世代发育持续时间为 < 1 年。推断的 队列研究 结构表明,单个季节性活动峰值可能包含多个重叠的 队列研究。例如,5月至8月的夏季成虫高峰可能包括早期的越冬成虫和后期以若虫形式取食的新成熟成虫。结论 这些发现强调,在对人类 发热伴血小板减少综合征 风险进行建模时,需要考虑人类蜱接触模式以及特定于地点和月份的时间尺度。

papers.title: A novel 17-plex multi-pathogen detection for rapid and accurate diagnosis of tick-borne diseases
papers.abstract: In recent years, anthropogenic ecological disruption has escalated tick-borne zoonoses; ticks transmit taxonomically diverse pathogens with overlapping clinical signs, challenging precise diagnosis and increasing risk of simultaneous detection in pooled samples. Despite advancements, current sequencing technologies, such as Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) assays, and antibody-based detection methods, are hampered by limitations including extended processing times and limited detection throughput. These constraints significantly hinder their effectiveness in high-throughput pathogen screening for animal or patient samples. To address these challenges, we developed an innovative multi-detection method based on the Multi-analyte Suspension Assay (MASA), enabling rapid and accurate diagnosis of a comprehensive panel of 17 vector-borne pathogens. This 17-plex panel comprises Rickettsia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Borrelia recurrentis, Babesia spp., Borrelia burgdorferi, Rickettsia prowazekii, Rickettsia heilongjiangensis, Orientia tsutsugamushi, Coxiella burnetii, Leptospira, Bartonella spp., Candidatus Ehrlichia erytraense, Hantaan Virus (HTNV), Seoul Virus (SEOV), Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV), Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV), and Tick-Borne Encephalitis Virus (TBEV). By combining this novel method with traditional techniques, including nested PCR and Real-Time Quantitative Reverse Transcription PCR (qRT-PCR), we achieved accurate detection of pathogens such as Rickettsia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, and SFTSV in tick samples. Notably, the technique revealed the co-existence of multiple pathogens within the same sample group, highlighting its ability in identifying co-detection of pathogens. Additionally, in suspected cases of tick-borne pathogen infection in febrile patients, the method quickly identified positive results for SFTSV and Rickettsia spp. These preliminary results suggest the potential of this method as a promising screening tool for clinical diagnostics, although larger-scale validation is warranted. This method provides a preliminary technical candidate approach for the development of more sensitive field-deployable detection tools.

source_records.title: A novel 17-plex multi-pathogen detection for rapid and accurate diagnosis of tick-borne diseases.
source_records.abstract: In recent years, anthropogenic ecological disruption has escalated tick-borne zoonoses; ticks transmit taxonomically diverse pathogens with overlapping clinical signs, challenging precise diagnosis and increasing risk of simultaneous detection in pooled samples. Despite advancements, current sequencing technologies, such as Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) assays, and antibody-based detection methods, are hampered by limitations including extended processing times and limited detection throughput. These constraints significantly hinder their effectiveness in high-throughput pathogen screening for animal or patient samples. To address these challenges, we developed an innovative multi-detection method based on the Multi-analyte Suspension Assay (MASA), enabling rapid and accurate diagnosis of a comprehensive panel of 17 vector-borne pathogens. This 17-plex panel comprises Rickettsia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Borrelia recurrentis, Babesia spp., Borrelia burgdorferi, Rickettsia prowazekii, Rickettsia heilongjiangensis, Orientia tsutsugamushi, Coxiella burnetii, Leptospira, Bartonella spp., Candidatus Ehrlichia erytraense, Hantaan Virus (HTNV), Seoul Virus (SEOV), Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV), Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV), and Tick-Borne Encephalitis Virus (TBEV). By combining this novel method with traditional techniques, including nested PCR and Real-Time Quantitative Reverse Transcription PCR (qRT-PCR), we achieved accurate detection of pathogens such as Rickettsia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, and SFTSV in tick samples. Notably, the technique revealed the co-existence of multiple pathogens within the same sample group, highlighting its ability in identifying co-detection of pathogens. Additionally, in suspected cases of tick-borne pathogen infection in febrile patients, the method quickly identified positive results for SFTSV and Rickettsia spp. These preliminary results suggest the potential of this method as a promising screening tool for clinical diagnostics, although larger-scale validation is warranted. This method provides a preliminary technical candidate approach for the development of more sensitive field-deployable detection tools.

analysis_zh.methods: 为了应对这些挑战,我们开发了一种基于多分析物悬浮测定 (MASA) 的创新多重检测方法,能够快速、准确地对 17 种 媒介 传播的病原体进行全面检测。通过将这种新方法与传统技术(包括巢式PCR和实时定量逆转录PCR(qRT-PCR))相结合,我们实现了对蜱样本中立克次体、嗜吞噬细胞无形体和SFTSV等病原体的准确检测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 值得注意的是,该技术揭示了同一样本组内多种病原体的共存,凸显了其识别病原体共检测的能力。此外,在发热患者疑似蜱媒病原体感染病例中,该方法快速鉴定出SFTSV和立克次体属阳性结果。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些初步结果表明,尽管需要进行更大规模的验证,但该方法作为临床诊断的有前途的筛选工具的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该方法为开发更灵敏的现场部署检测工具提供了初步的技术候选方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 然而,更大规模的验证是必要的。

papers.title: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome-associated viral sepsis: risk factors for critical illness and mortality and the prognostic value of urinalysis
papers.abstract: Background Since its identification in China in 2009, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) has emerged as an important tick-borne pathogen associated with substantial severity and mortality. Early recognition of patients at high risk of clinical deterioration or death remains challenging, particularly in resource-limited settings. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, 798 patients with laboratory-confirmed SFTSV infection were included, who were admitted to five tertiary hospitals in Jiangsu and Anhui provinces, China, between April 1, 2021, to October 31, 2024. Patients were classified as critical (n=271) or non-critical (n=527), and critically ill patients were further categorized as survivors (n=134) or non-survivors (n=137). Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, clinical manifestations, organ dysfunction, hematological and coagulation indices, biochemical markers, urinalysis findings, and arterial blood gas parameters were evaluated. Urinalysis included urinary protein, occult blood, glucose, bilirubin, urobilinogen, pH, and urinary red and white blood cell counts, among other routine parameters. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with critical illness and in-hospital mortality. Results Of 798 patients with SFTSV infection, 271 (34.0%) developed critical illness, of whom 137 (50.6%) died during hospitalization. The median age was 67 years [interquartile range (IQR) 58-73], and 87.3% resided in rural areas. Compared with non-critical patients, critically ill patients exhibited more pronounced hematological and coagulation abnormalities, biochemical evidence of organ injury, and urinary abnormalities, particularly proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria. Multivariable analysis identified age, neurological, renal, and respiratory dysfunction, direct bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), creatine kinase (CK) and D-dimer as independent factors associated with critical illness. Among critically ill patients, non-survivors had greater organ dysfunction and higher illness severity scores than survivors. Notably, urinalysis revealed a significantly higher frequency of urobilinogen positivity (25.5% vs. 13.4%, p = 0.012) and elevated urinary white blood cell (WBC) counts in non-survivors. Multivariable analysis further identified age, urinary urobilinogen positivity, and creatinine, as independent factors associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings suggest that selected urinary abnormalities may provide complementary information for mortality risk assessment in critically ill patients with SFTS. Conclusion SFTSV infection is a systemic disease characterized by profound hematological and coagulation disturbances together with progressive multiorgan dysfunction. Age, neurological, renal, and respiratory dysfunction and biochemical markers of organ injury were independently associated with critical illness, whereas advanced age and selected urinary abnormalities were independently associated with mortality among critically ill patients. These findings support comprehensive early assessment of organ dysfunction and routine laboratory and urinalysis monitoring for risk stratification and clinical management of SFTS.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates risk factors for critical illness and mortality in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) infection. It highlights the importance of early recognition of high-risk patients, particularly in resource-limited settings, and identifies age, neurological, renal, and respiratory dysfunction, along with specific biochemical and urinalysis markers, as independent predictors of critical illness and mortality. The findings suggest that urinary abnormalities, such as urobilinogen positivity and elevated white blood cell counts, may offer additional insights for risk assessment in critically ill SFTSV patients. The study is a retrospective multicenter analysis of 798 patients admitted to hospitals in Jiangsu and Anhui provinces between 2021 and 2024. While the study provides valuable insights into the clinical features and prognostic indicators of SFTSV, it does not report specific limitations, which may affect the confidence in its conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 自 2009 年在中国发现以来,发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 已成为一种与严重程度和 死亡率 相关的重要 蜱媒 病原体。早期识别临床恶化或死亡高风险的患者仍然具有挑战性,特别是在资源有限的环境中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项回顾性多中心研究中,纳入了2021年4月1日至2024年10月31日期间在中国江苏省和安徽省的5家三级医院收治的798名实验室确诊的SFTSV感染患者。患者被分为危重(n = 271)或非危重(n = 527),危重患者进一步分为幸存者(n = 134)或非幸存者(137)。
elements_zh.methods: 评估人口统计学特征、合并症、临床表现、器官功能障碍、血液学和凝血指数、生化标志物、尿液分析结果和动脉血气参数。进行多变量逻辑回归以确定与危重疾病和住院 死亡率 独立相关的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 798例SFTSV感染患者中,271例(34.0%)病情发展为危重,其中137例(50.6%)在住院期间死亡。危重患者表现出更明显的血液学和凝血异常、器官损伤的生化证据以及泌尿系统异常,特别是蛋白尿、血尿和糖尿。在重症患者中,非幸存者比幸存者有更严重的器官功能障碍和更高的疾病严重程度评分。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,选定的尿液异常可能为 死亡率 危重患者的 死亡率 风险评估提供补充信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持对器官功能障碍进行全面的早期评估以及常规实验室和尿液分析监测,以进行 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的风险分层和临床管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。

papers.title: LPC(16:0) and prothrombin time as mortality predictors in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with a high fatality rate. However, the impact of the SFTS virus (SFTSV) on host lipid metabolism and its relationship with the prognosis of patients remain unclear. To determine the lipid metabolism profile of SFTSV-infected and identify prognostic biomarkers, targeted lipidomics analysis was conducted on SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and serum samples from 71 subjects (including 15 healthy controls, 35 SFTS survivors, and 21 SFTS deceased patients) in this study. Our findings revealed that glycerophospholipid metabolism was the most significantly disrupted pathway in both SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and SFTS patients, with lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) species, including LPC(16:1), LPC(18:1), LPC(16:0), and LPC(18:0), showing decreased levels. Together with clinical parameters, prothrombin time (PT) and LPC(16:0) were further identified as prognostic factors, and the combined model incorporating these two markers predicted mortality with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.937. These findings provide a foundation for mortality prediction and mechanistic understanding of SFTS. IMPORTANCE Effective prognostic tools and targeted therapies for SFTS remain urgently needed, as current clinical management relies largely on supportive care and lacks reliable indicators for early risk stratification. This study enhances our understanding of lipid alterations following SFTSV infection, opens potential avenues for metabolism-targeted intervention, and may aid in assessing disease progression and guiding appropriate clinical interventions.

However, the impact of the SFTS virus (SFTSV) on host lipid metabolism and its relationship with the prognosis of patients remain unclear. To determine the lipid metabolism profile of SFTSV-infected and identify prognostic biomarkers, targeted lipidomics analysis was conducted on SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and serum samples from 71 subjects (including 15 healthy controls, 35 SFTS survivors, and 21 SFTS deceased patients) in this study. Our findings revealed that glycerophospholipid metabolism was the most significantly disrupted pathway in both SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and SFTS patients, with lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) species, including LPC(16:1), LPC(18:1), LPC(16:0), and LPC(18:0), showing decreased levels. Together with clinical parameters, prothrombin time (PT) and LPC(16:0) were further identified as prognostic factors, and the combined model incorporating these two markers predicted mortality with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.937. These findings provide a foundation for mortality prediction and mechanistic understanding of SFTS. IMPORTANCE Effective prognostic tools and targeted therapies for SFTS remain urgently needed, as current clinical management relies largely on supportive care and lacks reliable indicators for early risk stratification. This study enhances our understanding of lipid alterations following SFTSV infection, opens potential avenues for metabolism-targeted intervention, and may aid in assessing disease progression and guiding appropriate clinical interventions.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是一种新出现的 蜱媒 病毒性疾病,死亡率很高。然而,发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)对宿主脂质代谢的影响及其与患者预后的关系仍不清楚。为了确定SFTSV感染者的脂质代谢谱并确定预后生物标志物,本研究对SFTSV感染的Huh7细胞和71名受试者(包括15名健康对照、35名发热伴血小板减少综合征幸存者和21名发热伴血小板减少综合征死亡患者)的血清样本进行了靶向脂质组学分析。我们的研究结果表明,甘油磷脂代谢是SFTSV感染的Huh7细胞和发热伴血小板减少综合征患者中最显着破坏的途径,溶血磷脂酰胆碱(LPC)种类,包括LPC(16:1)、LPC(18:1)、LPC(16:0)和LPC(18:0),表现出水平下降。与临床参数一起,凝血酶原时间(PT)和LPC(16:0)被进一步确定为预后因素,并且结合这两个标志物的组合模型预测死亡率的曲线下面积(AUC)为0.937。这些发现为 死亡率 预测和 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的机制理解提供了基础。重要性仍然迫切需要 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的有效预后工具和靶向治疗,因为当前的临床管理主要依赖于支持性护理,并且缺乏早期风险分层的可靠指标。这项研究增强了我们对SFTSV感染后脂质变化的理解,为代谢靶向干预开辟了潜在途径,并可能有助于评估疾病进展和指导适当的临床干预。

papers.full_text: nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2357–2359 | 2357 Vaccine preparedness for the next emerging infectious disease crisis Florian Krammer Recent outbreaks with viruses such as Bundi­bugyo virus and Andes virus are a reminder that another pandemic can happen at any time. This Comment summarizes where we stand with pandemic preparedness from a vaccine perspective. During the COVID-19 pandemic, we witnessed vaccine develop­ment at its finest. Vaccines against the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 were developed at record speed and were made available within approximately 1 year after the outbreak started1. This swift devel­ opment of vaccines was facilitated by new technologies such as the mRNA vaccine platform2 but also by a wealth of exist­ ing knowledge because of many years of virology, vacci­nology and structural biology research. Much has happened since the COVID-19 pandemic. Technology has evolved, new insights into mechanisms of protection and basic immunology have been gained and regulatory and policy views have changed (Fig. 1), especially in the USA. Where does this leave us with vaccine preparedness for emerging pathogens? Mucosal immunity matters A clear lesson learned from the COVID-19 pandemic was that intramus­ cular vaccination can only imperfectly protect from infection with respiratory viruses per se and from onward transmission1. Vaccines that are administered via mucosal surfaces may be a better option to induce immunity in the upper respiratory tract to protect from infection with respiratory viruses. This was clearly identified as a gap, and funding agencies, including the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA), set out to support the development of mucosal vaccine approaches for COVID-19 (ref. 3). Unfortunately, funding for many of these vaccines was terminated or redirected to other projects owing to the policy decision that COVID-19 is no longer a priority. How­ ever, having infection- and transmission-blocking vaccines early in an outbreak with a respiratory virus would notably increase the effect of vaccines. Although several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are either still in development or already licensed outside the USA and Europe4,5, there is a large gap in terms of vaccine preparedness when it comes to mucosal vaccination routes. Having mucosal vaccines with clear immunological (and potentially mucosal) correlates of protection and established vaccine efficacy and safety on the market would increase confidence in these vaccine platforms and would likely enable early deployment during an outbreak or a pandemic. Broadly protective or strain-specific vaccines Studies of influenza virus and HIV-1 have shown that RNA viruses can evolve quickly. This was also observed with SARS-CoV-2. With the emergence of the Omicron variants, vaccines had to be updated to stay effective. However, updating vaccines to respond to emerging variants means always being one step behind the virus. This is a scenario with which we are very familiar from influenza virus vaccines. Owing to the antigenic variability of RNA viruses, the development of broadly protective vaccines has been the focus in the HIV-1 and influenza fields for many years but also became an important topic for SARS-CoV-2. The concept of broadly protective vaccines goes further than the idea of covering evolving virus variants. The idea has expanded to develop vaccines that potentially can protect from whole virus families, which would considerably increase pandemic preparedness. Although fund­ ing for such vaccines has been made available (for example, via the NIAID Collaborative Influenza Vaccine Innovation Centers program, the BARDA funding initiatives and the European Health and Digital Executive Agency), they have not progressed far enough to be used in case of an emergency. Further investment is urgently needed to advance these candidates and concepts through clinical development and real­ ize their potential as tools to combat evolving viral threats and future Comment https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02726-w Check for updates Broadly protective vs virus/strain- specific vaccines Mucosal vs injected vaccines Vaccine platform Vaccine acceptance Market Regulatory policy Manufacturing speed Funding policy Basic research Vaccine preparedness Vaccine Fig. 1 | Factors and aspects that influence epidemic and pandemic vaccine preparedness. Although technology has advanced, questions about broadly protective versus specific vaccines and mucosal vaccines remain. In addition, recent changes in funding and regulatory policy increase uncertainty for vaccine preparedness. nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2357–2359 | 2358 Comment pandemics. In addition, the regulatory pathway to get such vaccines licensed remains unclear. Vaccines need to be tested in phase 3 efficacy trials to show how well they protect against disease. To demonstrate that a vaccine is broadly protective, multi-year trials to show efficacy in seasons with antigenic changes are likely needed, and such trials may be prohibitively expensive. Furthermore, demonstrating efficacy against pathogens that are not yet circulating in humans is impossible, making it difficult to claim universal protection against future pathogens with pandemic potential. For pandemic preparedness, strain-matched vac­ cines that can be generated rapidly after the emergence of a new virus currently seems to be favored over the development of broadly protec­ tive vaccines (for example, https://cepi.net/100-days). Although this is of course also a good approach, it would be better to have vaccines ready before a new outbreak even starts and not months later, which is something that a broadly protective or universal vaccine could deliver. Pandemic influenza breakthroughs The recent pan-zootic with highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b influenza virus and its spillover into many mammalian species has raised concerns about the potential of this virus to cause a pandemic6. Fortunately, recent developments have enhanced pandemic influenza vaccine preparedness. For influenza vaccines, a correlate of protection accepted by regulators exists — the hemagglutination inhibition titer — although several other validated correlates of protection have also been established by academic researchers7. If a vaccine manufacturer has a licensed seasonal influenza virus vaccine on the market, the same technology can be used to manufacture a vaccine for an emerging pandemic influenza virus strain and get it to the market based on this correlate, instead of performing time-consuming phase 3 field efficacy trials first. Although effectiveness must be confirmed later, this step saves a lot of time during an outbreak. So far, this pathway has been open to manufacturers who are producing influenza vaccines using traditional technologies, such as split-inactivated vaccines. To update these vaccines to a new pandemic strain can be time-consuming. This process can be faster using the mRNA platform, but until recently, no mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccines were available, meaning that this quick strain-change pathway was not open to the mRNA technol­ ogy. The recent licensure of an mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine from Moderna (mFLUSIVA in the USA; mCOMBRIAX in the European Union) changed this8. Although the benefits of an mRNA-based sea­ sonal influenza vaccine compared with conventional vaccines remain debated, the advantage in terms of speed in case of a pandemic is a game changer. Using the mechanism of a strain change from seasonal strains to a pandemic strain in combination with the mRNA technology may make it possible to have a matched pandemic influenza vaccine ready for use in the population within 3 months. The Bundibugyo virus outbreak as a test In May 2026, an outbreak with Bundibugyo virus was reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)9. This outbreak is still ongo­ ing, case numbers are growing and it has now become the second larg­ est outbreak of Ebola disease in recorded history. Although vaccines against another virus species, Ebola virus (formerly known as Zaire ebolavirus), are licensed and available, strain-matched vaccines for Bundibugyo virus had not been clinically developed10. This crisis in the DRC serves as test for post-COVID-19 pandemic vaccine preparedness. So far, two vaccines have moved into clinical evaluation. The first phase 1 trial, based on an adenovirus vector (ChAdOx1-BDBV-GP), began in July in the UK11. A second trial, with an mRNA vaccine, was initiated in August in Canada (mRNA-1469, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07737717). How long it takes to move these vaccines forward in the clinical pipeline, whether they are successful, and if they are fast enough to be used in the current outbreak remain to be determined. It is, however, notewor­ thy that these two vaccines are based on the same technologies that delivered the first COVID-19 vaccines. The value of basic research for vaccine preparedness Another aspect that needs to be mentioned is basic research that is being conducted to better understand emerging viruses that have so far gained little interest, especially viruses belonging to the Bunyaviri­ cetes. This class includes viruses such as severe fever with thrombocy­ topenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHVF), Toscana virus (TOSV), Heartland virus, Shamonda virus, Yezo virus12 and Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV)13, as well as hantaviruses such as Andes virus14. Some of these viruses are already human-to-human transmissible and have caused concerning outbreaks, such as the Andes virus outbreak in May on the cruise ship MV Hondius15. The spike proteins of these viruses were not well understood, making vaccine design complicated. Recent advances in understanding the molecular biology, structural biology and antigenicity of these viruses, partially funded by the excellent NIAID Research and Development of Vaccines and Monoclonal Antibodies for Pandemic Preparedness (ReVAMPP) program, have started to change that. Using new technolo­ gies and insights, vaccines against these challenging targets can now potentially also be developed quickly if needed, highlighting the need for and value of basic research. Conclusions The obvious question is, are we now, after the COVID-19 pandemic, better prepared for coming epidemics and pandemics in respect to vac­ cines? The answer is not a simple yes or no. Technology has advanced, our understanding of virus biology has markedly increased and COVID- 19 has shown us that vaccines can be developed quickly if needed and if an effort is made by all stakeholders. However, there is much still to learn; from basic research and clinical testing to manufacturing and regulatory policies. Importantly, funding policies and regulatory policies are changing in parts of the world, partially influenced by the anti-vaccine movement that now has advocates within governments. It is unclear what the long-term effect of these changes is on vaccine development and pandemic preparedness. To demonstrate that a vaccine is broadly protective, multi-year trials to show efficacy in seasons with antigenic changes are likely needed, and such trials may be prohibitively expensive. Furthermore, demonstrating efficacy against pathogens that are not yet circulating in humans is impossible, making it difficult to claim universal protection against future pathogens with pandemic potential. For pandemic preparedness, strain-matched vac­ cines that can be generated rapidly after the emergence of a new virus currently seems to be favored over the development of broadly protec­ tive vaccines (for example, https://cepi.net/100-days). Although this is of course also a good approach, it would be better to have vaccines ready before a new outbreak even starts and not months later, which is something that a broadly protective or universal vaccine could deliver. Pandemic influenza breakthroughs The recent pan-zootic with highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b influenza virus and its spillover into many mammalian species has raised concerns about the potential of this virus to cause a pandemic6. Fortunately, recent developments have enhanced pandemic influenza vaccine preparedness. For influenza vaccines, a correlate of protection accepted by regulators exists — the hemagglutination inhibition titer — although several other validated correlates of protection have also been established by academic researchers7. If a vaccine manufacturer has a licensed seasonal influenza virus vaccine on the market, the same technology can be used to manufacture a vaccine for an emerging pandemic influenza virus strain and get it to the market based on this correlate, instead of performing time-consuming phase 3 field efficacy trials first. Although effectiveness must be confirmed later, this step saves a lot of time during an outbreak. So far, this pathway has been open to manufacturers who are producing influenza vaccines using traditional technologies, such as split-inactivated vaccines. To update these vaccines to a new pandemic strain can be time-consuming. This process can be faster using the mRNA platform, but until recently, no mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccines were available, meaning that this quick strain-change pathway was not open to the mRNA technol­ ogy. The recent licensure of an mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine from Moderna (mFLUSIVA in the USA; mCOMBRIAX in the European Union) changed this8. Although the benefits of an mRNA-based sea­ sonal influenza vaccine compared with conventional vaccines remain debated, the advantage in terms of speed in case of a pandemic is a game changer. Using the mechanism of a strain change from seasonal strains to a pandemic strain in combination with the mRNA technology may make it possible to have a matched pandemic influenza vaccine ready for use in the population within 3 months. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improved vaccine preparedness for emerging infectious diseases, highlighting the importance of learning from past outbreaks such as Bundi­bugyo virus and Andes virus to better respond to future pandemics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary summarizing the current state of pandemic preparedness from a vaccine perspective, focusing on the lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic and the evolution of vaccine technologies and policies.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review of vaccine development processes, including the use of new technologies like the mRNA vaccine platform, and an analysis of the factors that influenced vaccine development and deployment during the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.main_results: The main results indicate that vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 were developed rapidly and made available within about 1 year after the outbreak began, but there remains a significant gap in vaccine preparedness for mucosal vaccination routes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that mucosal vaccines could offer better protection against respiratory viruses, and they highlight the novelty of recognizing the importance of mucosal immunity in pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that having mucosal vaccines with established efficacy and safety could enhance confidence in these platforms and enable quicker deployment during future outbreaks or pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a commentary and does not present original data, but the evidence is strong due to its focus on well-documented lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic and current vaccine development trends.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary discusses the importance of vaccine preparedness for emerging infectious diseases, emphasizing lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights the role of mucosal immunity in protecting against respiratory viruses and the need for further development of mucosal vaccine platforms. The authors note that while SARS-CoV-2 vaccines were developed quickly, there is still a gap in mucosal vaccine preparedness. They suggest that having effective mucosal vaccines could improve pandemic response. The study is based on a review of existing knowledge and current vaccine technologies, and it identifies limitations in the current state of vaccine development for emerging pathogens. The evidence is strong due to its focus on well-documented experiences and policy changes, but the commentary does not present original data.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Urinary Urobilinogen and Organ Impairment Predict Mortality in Severe SFTSV Infections by November 25, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Urinary Urobilinogen and Organ Impairment Predict Mortality in Severe SFTSV Infections Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a retrospective multicenter study published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, researchers reported that urinary urobilinogen positivity, elevated serum creatinine, and advanced age serve as independent prognostic markers of in-hospital mortality among critically ill patients suffering from severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus infection. Conducted across five tertiary medical centers in China, the investigation analyzed hundreds of clinical cases to determine how organ dysfunction, routine blood parameters, and standard urinalysis findings can aid clinicians in distinguishing severe clinical trajectories from non-critical presentations. The infection is characterized by systemic inflammation, severe hematological disturbances, and progressive multiorgan failure, presenting substantial morbidity and mortality. To clarify the risk factors linked to disease progression, the investigators evaluated 798 patients with laboratory-confirmed SFTS virus infections who were admitted between April 1, 2021, and October 31, 2024. Within this patient population, the median age was 67 years, with an interquartile range spanning from 58 to 73 years, and 87.3 percent of the individuals resided in rural regions. For comparative analysis, the research team stratified the overall cohort into 527 non-critical patients and 271 critically ill patients, representing 34.0 percent of the total group. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Hematological, coagulation, and biochemical profiles were systematically measured alongside comprehensive urinalysis testing. The observational data showed marked differences between illness severity groups, as critically ill patients demonstrated significantly more pronounced hematological and coagulation abnormalities, biochemical evidence of severe organ injury, and elevated frequencies of urinary abnormalities, notably proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria. Using multivariable logistic regression to control for confounding variables, the authors established that older age, direct bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase, creatine kinase, and D-dimer concentrations, alongside documented neurological, renal, and respiratory dysfunctions, were independently associated with the development of critical illness. Discover more Donate to Research Find Study Aids Healthy Among the 271 critically ill individuals, in-hospital mortality was severe, with 137 patients dying during hospitalization, reflecting a 50.6 percent mortality rate within the intensive cohort, while 134 individuals survived. Non-survivors presented with greater degrees of organ failure and markedly higher clinical severity scores than survivors. Urinalysis demonstrated notable differences between these two subsets: positive urinary urobilinogen was detected in 25.5 percent of non-survivors compared to 13.4 percent of survivors, an association achieving statistical significance at a p-value of 0.012, accompanied by elevated urinary white blood cell counts. In multivariable logistic regression modeling focusing on critically ill patients, older age, elevated serum creatinine, and positive urinary urobilinogen tests remained independently associated with fatal outcomes. The study authors, led by corresponding author Zhimin Tao and collaborating investigators from institutions including the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangsu University and Nanjing Medical University, concluded that SFTS manifests as a complex viral sepsis marked by profound multiorgan involvement. The researchers emphasized that integrating routine urinalysis monitoring with standard blood biochemistry provides valuable, complementary prognostic information for mortality risk stratification, offering an accessible tool for clinical management. However, because the investigation relied on a retrospective design, the authors noted that prospective clinical validation remains necessary before these findings can be established across broader healthcare settings. news.content_original: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Urinary Urobilinogen and Organ Impairment Predict Mortality in Severe SFTSV Infections by November 25, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Urinary Urobilinogen and Organ Impairment Predict Mortality in Severe SFTSV Infections Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a retrospective multicenter study published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, researchers reported that urinary urobilinogen positivity, elevated serum creatinine, and advanced age serve as independent prognostic markers of in-hospital mortality among critically ill patients suffering from severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus infection. Conducted across five tertiary medical centers in China, the investigation analyzed hundreds of clinical cases to determine how organ dysfunction, routine blood parameters, and standard urinalysis findings can aid clinicians in distinguishing severe clinical trajectories from non-critical presentations. The infection is characterized by systemic inflammation, severe hematological disturbances, and progressive multiorgan failure, presenting substantial morbidity and mortality. To clarify the risk factors linked to disease progression, the investigators evaluated 798 patients with laboratory-confirmed SFTS virus infections who were admitted between April 1, 2021, and October 31, 2024. Within this patient population, the median age was 67 years, with an interquartile range spanning from 58 to 73 years, and 87.3 percent of the individuals resided in rural regions. For comparative analysis, the research team stratified the overall cohort into 527 non-critical patients and 271 critically ill patients, representing 34.0 percent of the total group. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Hematological, coagulation, and biochemical profiles were systematically measured alongside comprehensive urinalysis testing. The observational data showed marked differences between illness severity groups, as critically ill patients demonstrated significantly more pronounced hematological and coagulation abnormalities, biochemical evidence of severe organ injury, and elevated frequencies of urinary abnormalities, notably proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria. Using multivariable logistic regression to control for confounding variables, the authors established that older age, direct bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase, creatine kinase, and D-dimer concentrations, alongside documented neurological, renal, and respiratory dysfunctions, were independently associated with the development of critical illness. Discover more Donate to Research Find Study Aids Healthy Among the 271 critically ill individuals, in-hospital mortality was severe, with 137 patients dying during hospitalization, reflecting a 50.6 percent mortality rate within the intensive cohort, while 134 individuals survived. Non-survivors presented with greater degrees of organ failure and markedly higher clinical severity scores than survivors. Urinalysis demonstrated notable differences between these two subsets: positive urinary urobilinogen was detected in 25.5 percent of non-survivors compared to 13.4 percent of survivors, an association achieving statistical significance at a p-value of 0.012, accompanied by elevated urinary white blood cell counts. In multivariable logistic regression modeling focusing on critically ill patients, older age, elevated serum creatinine, and positive urinary urobilinogen tests remained independently associated with fatal outcomes. The study authors, led by corresponding author Zhimin Tao and collaborating investigators from institutions including the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangsu University and Nanjing Medical University, concluded that SFTS manifests as a complex viral sepsis marked by profound multiorgan involvement. The researchers emphasized that integrating routine urinalysis monitoring with standard blood biochemistry provides valuable, complementary prognostic information for mortality risk stratification, offering an accessible tool for clinical management. However, because the investigation relied on a retrospective design, the authors noted that prospective clinical validation remains necessary before these findings can be established across broader healthcare settings. news.content_zh: 2026 年 11 月 25 日发表在《细胞和感染微生物学前沿》上的一项研究确定了 死亡率 (SFTSV) 感染中 死亡率 的关键危险因素。该研究在中国五个三级医疗中心进行,分析了2021年4月1日至2024年10月31日期间收治的798名患者,其中87.3%来自农村地区。研究结果显示,尿胆原阳性、血清肌酐升高和高龄是危重患者住院 死亡率 的独立预测因素。271 名重症患者中,死亡 137 人,死亡率 率为 50.6%。非幸存者表现出更严重的器官衰竭和更高的临床严重程度评分。由陶志民及其同事领导的这项研究强调了将尿液分析与血液生化相结合对于 死亡率 风险分层的重要性。然而,作者指出,为了更广泛地应用这些结果,前瞻性验证是必要的。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Clinical Scoring Tool Distinguishes Lethal Viral Infection From Scrub Typhus Without Eschar by November 25, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Clinical Scoring Tool Distinguishes Lethal Viral Infection From Scrub Typhus Without Eschar Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A retrospective clinical evaluation conducted in South Korea has demonstrated that a straightforward six-variable scoring system can accurately differentiate severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome from scrub typhus without relying on the presence of a characteristic eschar. The study, conducted at Jeju National University Hospital and analyzing records through December thirty-first 2024, evaluated the diagnostic utility of the Tick-borne Infection Severity Score across two hundred and ninety-five adult patients presenting with confirmed vector-borne infections. In East Asia, both severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, caused by the bunyavirus Bandavirus dabieense, and tsutsugamushi disease, caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, present formidable diagnostic dilemmas during overlapping seasonal surges. While scrub typhus responds rapidly to empirical antimicrobial regimens such as doxycycline and carries a case fatality below one percent, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome carries mortality rates ranging between ten and thirty percent, lacks established antiviral therapies, and poses grave risks of nosocomial transmission to healthcare workers exposed to infectious blood or bodily secretions. The clinical imperative for an eschar-independent diagnostic rule arises directly from the biological limitations of physical examination findings in clinical practice. Furthermore, while cutaneous rash is another potential distinguishing feature, it does not occur universally in tsutsugamushi disease and is exceedingly rare in acute severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome. The architecture of the scoring system assigns two points for the absence of a cutaneous rash, two points for altered mental status, two points for a platelet count below one hundred thousand per microliter, three points for a white blood cell count below four thousand per microliter, three points for a serum C-reactive protein concentration equal to or below three milligrams per deciliter, and one point for a lymphocyte proportion exceeding thirty percent. These specific clinical and laboratory cut-offs directly capture the divergent pathophysiological trajectories that characterize the two vector-borne infections. In severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, viral tropism directed against bone marrow megakaryocytes, monocytes, and vascular endothelial cells leads to marked bone marrow suppression, generating profound leukopenia, severe thrombocytopenia, and relative lymphocytosis resulting from atypical reactive lymphocytes and peripheral neutrophil depletion. In sharp contrast, Orientia tsutsugamushi produces disseminated microvascular endothelial inflammation accompanied by an intense systemic acute-phase reactant cascade, typically manifested by substantial elevations in serum C-reactive protein and preserved or elevated white blood cell counts. To evaluate the real-world performance of the score, investigators assembled a retrospective cohort comprising one hundred and one patients with reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome treated between 2013 and 2024, alongside one hundred and ninety-four patients with tsutsugamushi disease treated during the intervals of 2003 through 2012 or 2022 through 2024. The diagnostic case definition for scrub typhus required a fourfold or greater elevation in indirect immunofluorescence antibody titers in paired sera or a single diagnostic titer of at least one to four hundred. Available patient ages across the combined cohort spanned from eighteen to ninety-two years, with a median age of sixty-three years in the viral cohort and sixty years in the scrub typhus cohort. The researchers extracted clinical and biochemical parameters recorded during initial hospital encounters using standardized case report forms approved by the Institutional Review Board of Jeju National University Hospital, which granted an informed consent waiver because the investigation utilized de-identified medical records collected during routine emergency care. Among two hundred and forty-one complete cases with full scoring parameters available, the diagnostic rule demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.985, with a ninety-five percent confidence interval ranging from 0.973 to 0.997. When applying a threshold of five points or higher, the system yielded an overall diagnostic sensitivity of 99.0 percent, identifying ninety-nine of one hundred confirmed cases of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, alongside an overall specificity of 84.4 percent, correctly classifying one hundred and nineteen of one hundred and forty-one scrub typhus patients. At this operational cut-off, the calculated positive predictive value reached 81.8 percent and the negative predictive value reached 99.2 percent within the study cohort. When evaluated at a higher operational threshold of eight points or higher, the rule achieved a specificity of 97.2 percent and a sensitivity of 90.0 percent, with ninety of one hundred viral cases scoring in the highest diagnostic stratum compared to only four scrub typhus cases. The study also examined the individual contribution of physical cutaneous signs through detailed sensitivity and ablation analyses. In the cohort, cutaneous rash was documented in 127 of 180 scrub typhus patients with recorded skin assessments, representing 70.6 percent, whereas rash was entirely absent across all one hundred and one patients presenting with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome. Similarly, an eschar was documented in 122 of 153 scrub typhus patients, representing 79.7 percent, while thirty-one patients had confirmed negative eschar evaluations and forty-one records lacked documentation. When researchers conducted an exploratory ablation analysis that removed the two points assigned for rash absence, the diagnostic area under the curve across the identical two hundred and forty-one complete patients declined from 0.985 to 0.970, a reduction that achieved statistical significance with a p-value of 0.012. Furthermore, in a subgroup of one hundred and twenty-nine patients with confirmed absence of an eschar, the score maintained an area under the curve of 0.987, confirming its discriminatory robustness when pathognomonic mite lesions cannot be identified. Direct pairwise comparisons against previously published diagnostic scores established the relative clinical merits and trade-offs of the evaluated scoring framework. In an identical complete-case sample of two hundred and forty-one patients, the six-variable system demonstrated a statistically superior area under the curve of 0.985 compared to 0.967 achieved by the three-variable Park score, with a paired comparison p-value of 0.003. Although the Park rule requires only white blood cell count, platelet count, and C-reactive protein, its published threshold of two or more points yielded a sensitivity of only 87.0 percent alongside a specificity of 95.0 percent, whereas the evaluated score at a cut-off of five achieved higher sensitivity at 99.0 percent. In a smaller subset of one hundred and eighteen patients with available specialized measurements, the score was compared with the four-item Sul model, which incorporates activated partial thromboplastin time and creatine kinase. In this group, the evaluated score attained an area under the curve of 0.992 compared to 0.971 for the Sul model, though the difference did not achieve statistical significance with an exploratory p-value of 0.058. The comparative analysis with the Sul scoring model highlighted substantial real-world data missingness that illustrates the practical logistical advantages of simpler bedside laboratory criteria. While creatine kinase and specialized coagulation panels were routinely ordered for ninety-four of one hundred and one patients presenting with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, treating clinicians obtained creatine kinase testing in only thirty of one hundred and ninety-four patients managed for tsutsugamushi disease. Because the Sul model necessitates specialized coagulation and muscle enzyme determinations that are frequently omitted during routine outpatient evaluations of milder febrile illnesses, its application was restricted to a highly selected subset of patients. In contrast, the evaluated six-variable scoring system relies exclusively on standardized complete blood count parameters with leukocyte differential and serum C-reactive protein concentrations, rendering it broadly feasible across resource-limited community clinics and primary emergency departments where specialized emergency assays are unavailable. In parallel computational investigations, researchers developed supervised machine-learning pipelines across eighty-nine held-out testing cases to evaluate how the fixed clinical rule performed against complex multivariable algorithms. A penalized logistic regression model trained on sixteen demographic, laboratory, and clinical variables attained a test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.989, achieving a sensitivity of 90.0 percent and a specificity of 94.9 percent at a standard decision probability threshold of 0.5. When the selected machine-learning model and the bedside scoring rule were evaluated on identical paired test patients who possessed complete scoring data, the machine-learning pipeline produced an area under the curve of 0.987 compared to 0.979 for the integer score. Crucially, the study established a stark clinical dissociation between initial diagnostic classification accuracy and individual patient prognostic risk stratification. Within the severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome cohort, the diagnostic scoring rule performed poorly when predicting in-hospital mortality, yielding an area under the curve of only 0.659, and failed to predict critical illness, producing an area under the curve of 0.561. In sharp contrast, baseline assessment using the Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score strongly predicted both in-hospital mortality, with an area under the curve of 0.789, and progression to critical illness, achieving an area under the curve of 0.835, which proved significantly superior to the diagnostic rule with a p-value of 0.010. Overall in-hospital mortality occurred in eleven of one hundred and one viral cases, representing 10.9 percent, compared to only one death among one hundred and ninety-four scrub typhus patients, representing 0.5 percent, while critical illness developed in twenty-one viral cases and five scrub typhus cases. This functional divergence between disease discrimination and clinical prognosis stems directly from underlying pathophysiology, as early hematological suppression reflects specific cellular viral tropism rather than the irreversible anatomical multi-organ failure that drives clinical mortality. Consequently, the authors emphasized that the evaluated scoring rubric must function strictly as an early emergency triage filter rather than a prognostic tool or disposition determinant. The scoring pathway is intended to identify patients requiring urgent viral isolation precautions, immediate blood reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction testing, and targeted empirical antimicrobial coverage, while established physiological organ failure scores such as the Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score must remain the primary basis for intensive care unit triage, hemodynamic vasopressor management, and continuous renal replacement therapy. The authors outlined several critical methodological limitations that circumscribe the immediate generalizability of their conclusions. First, the investigation was conducted as a single-center retrospective analysis situated within Jeju Island, a recognized hyperendemic insular setting in South Korea with distinctive agricultural exposure patterns and referral dynamics that may not mirror mainland medical centers. Second, the sampling periods across the two patient populations were partially non-contemporaneous, reflecting evolving diagnostic access, historical changes in testing kits, and changing regional surveillance practices. Third, selective clinical testing of specialized enzyme and coagulation parameters in tsutsugamushi disease caused substantial data missingness that limited comparator evaluations. Finally, because the scoring rule originated from preliminary observations on overlapping local patients and the cohort experienced only eleven fatal viral events, the authors emphasized that prospective external validation in diverse multi-center cohorts is essential before the scoring rubric can be formally implemented across wider clinical practice. analysis.brief_en: A study conducted at Jeju National University Hospital in South Korea has developed a six-variable clinical scoring tool to distinguish severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Bandavirus dabieense, from scrub typhus without relying on the presence of an eschar. The tool was evaluated on 295 adult patients with confirmed vector-borne infections, including 101 SFTS cases and 194 scrub typhus cases. The diagnostic system demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.985, with high sensitivity (99.0%) and specificity (84.4%) when using a five-point threshold. At an eight-point threshold, the specificity increased to 97.2% and sensitivity to 90.0%. The study highlights the importance of an eschar-independent diagnostic method due to the biological limitations of physical examination findings. Cutaneous rash was absent in all SFTS patients but present in 70.6% of scrub typhus patients. The researchers also noted methodological limitations, including non-contemporaneous sampling periods and evolving diagnostic practices, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The tool's performance was further validated using a penalized logistic regression model, achieving a test area under the curve of 0.989.

news.title_zh: 临床评分工具可区分致命的病毒感染和无焦痂的恙虫病
news.source_body_en: A study conducted at Jeju National University Hospital in South Korea has developed a six-variable clinical scoring tool to distinguish severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Bandavirus dabieense, from scrub typhus without relying on the presence of an eschar. The tool was evaluated on 295 adult patients with confirmed vector-borne infections, including 101 SFTS cases and 194 scrub typhus cases. The diagnostic system demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.985, with high sensitivity (99.0%) and specificity (84.4%) when using a five-point threshold. At an eight-point threshold, the specificity increased to 97.2% and sensitivity to 90.0%. The study highlights the importance of an eschar-independent diagnostic method due to the biological limitations of physical examination findings. Cutaneous rash was absent in all SFTS patients but present in 70.6% of scrub typhus patients. The researchers also noted methodological limitations, including non-contemporaneous sampling periods and evolving diagnostic practices, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The tool's performance was further validated using a penalized logistic regression model, achieving a test area under the curve of 0.989.
news.content_zh: 韩国济州国立大学医院进行的一项研究开发了一种六变量临床评分工具,可以在不依赖焦痂的情况下区分由达比班达病毒引起的严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 和恙虫病。该工具对 295 名确诊为 媒介 传播感染的成年患者进行了评估,其中包括 101 例 发热伴血小板减少综合征 病例和 194 例恙虫病病例。该诊断系统的受试者工作特征曲线下面积为 0.985,在使用五点阈值时具有高灵敏度 (99.0%) 和特异度 (84.4%)。在八点阈值下,特异性增加至 97.2%,敏感性增加至 90.0%。由于体检结果的生物学局限性,该研究强调了不依赖于焦痂的诊断方法的重要性。所有 发热伴血小板减少综合征 患者均未出现皮肤皮疹,但 70.6% 的恙虫病患者出现皮肤皮疹。研究人员还指出了方法学的局限性,包括非同期采样周期和不断发展的诊断实践,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。使用惩罚逻辑回归模型进一步验证了该工具的性能,达到了 0.989 的曲线下测试面积。

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection by November 24, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Platelet-Derived Vesicles Drive Macrophage Pyroptosis in Dabie Bandavirus Infection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Extracellular vesicles released by platelets during Dabie bandavirus infection directly trigger macrophage pyroptosis and amplify inflammatory responses, according to findings published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Dabie bandavirus causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, an emerging tick-borne infectious disease characterized by remarkably increased morbidity and mortality across East Asia. In clinical settings, thrombocytopenia represents a hallmark pathogenic event and an established independent predictor of multi-organ failure and poor clinical outcomes. Although Dabie bandavirus is known to bind to and replicate within host platelets, the precise contribution of activated platelets to disease pathogenesis has remained elusive. The researchers identified platelet-derived extracellular vesicles induced by Dabie bandavirus, designated DPEVs, as critical mediators of immune dysregulation. Upon viral activation, platelets release abundant vesicles that markedly heighten virus-driven inflammation while driving recipient macrophages into a distinct pro-inflammatory and pyroptosis-prone state. When compared directly with extracellular vesicles generated through physical disruption, DPEVs displayed significantly enhanced immunostimulatory capacity. Mechanistically, the study showed that DPEVs compromise mitochondrial integrity and stimulate the production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species inside macrophages, thereby triggering the downstream pyroptotic death program. This sequence defines a previously unrecognized pathogenic axis linking viral platelet activation, extracellular vesicle signaling, mitochondrial injury, and macrophagic pyroptosis during Dabie bandavirus infection. Beyond promoting inflammatory damage, DPEVs incorporated viral components, suggesting a potential dual role in mediating both inflammatory amplification and viral dissemination. By establishing a direct mechanistic link between thrombocytopenia and clinical severity in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, the findings position these virus-induced extracellular vesicles as key amplifiers of inflammation with notable potential value as clinical biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
